At the cell, Cell::check_models_promoted (backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/cell.rs:2645) admits a plan's inline DistilledModel only when that manifest names it at its digest, and qip-edge-node's StrategyInstaller (backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/strategies.rs) deploys a StrategyPlan read from the node's disk only when its bytes match the payload's compiled_plan PlanDigest. compiled_plan is never produced by the centre, so on a deployed node no strategy plan ever installs. | PARTIAL | The strategy pack has a consumer (StrategyInstaller) but no central producer: pending_policy never fills compiled_plan, so a deployed cell installs no plan. LocalQueue (the path that actually sheds a hot stream) is constructed only in qip-streaming's own tests; in production the shedding that runs is EventLog's retention-class eviction. qip-transport's outbound queue refuses uniformly under pressure. |  | P0 | A unit test asserting creating a stream without a StreamPolicy (or missing any of its fields) is refused -- does not exist. ## REFLEX

| REFLEX-001 | Reflex decisions run within the Lane 0 time scale | The SLO target exists and is honestly tracked as unmeasured: qip_observability::slo declares "wire-to-first-order-p99" (target 0.99, threshold 1.3ms) and "strategy-evaluation-p99"/"arrival-dispersion-p99" alongside it; qip_kernel::blueprint_objectives::unmeasured() classifies exactly these three as Unmeasured::NeedsReleaseTiming with the reason 'a p99 in microseconds or low milliseconds measures the container it is taken on unless the build is a release one and the hardware is quiet'. No benchmark harness computes an actual market-event-to-decision p99/p99.9 on target hardware anywhere in the tree. Separately, qip-acceptance/tests/performance.rs times the cell's in-memory pass in isolation (a debug-profile, single-thread mean under a 5,000us ceiling per Cell::work pass, and a per-pass scaling ratio), and its own header says tick-to-order latency is deliberately not measured. In the deployable, qip-edge-node runs one run_pass per accepted TCP connection on its health port (main.rs serve loop), after the halt poll, Cell::flush and the mesh exchange, so the running node reacts to market state at probe cadence, not on the event. | PARTIAL | No benchmark exists that replays a recorded session through a cell on the target machine shape and reports a real market-event-to-decision p99/p99.9 per venue shard; the objective is declared and honestly marked unmeasured (needs_release_timing) rather than falsely reported as met, but nothing produces the figure the requirement asks the build to fail on. Before any benchmark question: the deployable is not event-driven. qip-edge-node calls run_pass once per accepted health-probe connection, so its market-event-to-decision latency is the probe interval (seconds). A feed-driven pass loop is a prerequisite for the Lane 0 budget to be meetable at all, and the performance.rs figures (mean, debug, per stage) are not p99/p99.9 and not per venue shard. |  | P0 | Needed: a release-mode benchmark on quiet target hardware replaying a recorded session through qip_edge::Cell and feeding qip_observability::slo's wire-to-first-order-p99/p99.9 with a real figure, failing the build if either leaves 10ms. Today only qip-acceptance/tests/slo.rs proves the target is declared and unmeasured is reported honestly. | E04 |
| REFLEX-002 | Nothing remote stands between a venue event and the local order | qip_edge::Cell::on_bytes and Cell::work touch memory and arithmetic only (module doc backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/lib.rs:16-19; grep finds no std::net/std::fs/TcpStream in cell.rs). Cell::flush is the one cell call that may block, draining the journal to a Mirror. In the deployable, qip-edge-node's serve loop runs, on one thread and per accepted health-probe connection: the halt/region polls, Cell::flush to the configured store, the mesh exchange with the central plane (capital downlink poll, policy poll, uplink publish of the PREVIOUS pass's report, each blocking with a timeout), and only then run_pass. The simulated venue event is ingested inside run_pass (feed.publish -> Cell::on_bytes) and decided in the same call, so nothing remote sits between ingest and the paper order; but the start of each pass waits on the exchange and the flush. | PARTIAL | No dedicated test drives the requirement's own verification method: black-holing the Fabric/centre/model endpoints and a peer, then replaying a simulated venue event and asserting unchanged decision latency and an unchanged order. The invariant is proven today by code inspection (no I/O in the hot functions) plus adjacent tests (no-LLM reachability, mesh dead-letter/circuit-breaker), not by one test exercising this exact chaos scenario. qip-edge's own crate-level dependency graph does include qip-transport (for the separate, non-hot-path mesh module), so a naive crate-reachability architecture test of the kind the verification method describes would not by itself prove the invariant; it would need to be scoped to the on_bytes/work call graph. Also: in the running node the blocking mesh exchange and Cell::flush precede each run_pass on the same thread, so a stalled (not refused) centre delays when the next venue event is ingested by up to the transport timeouts; the requirement's 'unchanged decision latency' under a stalled peer is therefore unproven and probably false for event arrival time. And the node binary links qip-storage (with a GCS client, for the journal mirror) as well as qip-transport, so the crate-level 'no network client on the tick-to-order path' assertion would fail today unless scoped to the Cell::on_bytes/work call graph. |  | P0 | Needed: a chaos test that stalls/blackholes the mesh peer and any model endpoint, replays a simulated venue event through run_pass, and asserts the produced order and its latency are unchanged versus a healthy-peer run. Today: backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/tests/mesh.rs's dead-letter/circuit-open tests plus architecture.rs's no-LLM-reachability test. | E01 |
| REFLEX-003 | Regional nodes share compressed state with their peers | qip_edge::mesh::CellUplink pushes a CellStateDelta to one configured peer (mesh.rs:423 `peer: String`) and qip_edge::mesh::{PolicyDownlink, CapitalDownlink} pull signed policy/capital payloads from the same peer. In this build that peer is the central plane (qip-kernel's CentralPlane), not another regional cell — the exchange is hub-and-spoke through the centre, not a direct cell-to-cell channel. | PARTIAL | The requirement asks for direct peer-to-peer exchange between regional nodes ('exchange ... directly with peer nodes'); the in-tree mesh is a single uplink/downlink pair addressed at one peer, used in production as cell<->centre. | EXEC-037 | Orders, cancels and fills move between node and venue on the hot path | The direct path exists in its permitted (paper) form: qip_edge::cell::Cell::work sends orders straight to the node's in-process SimulatedGateway (no Fabric broker, regional service or other region between them), and fills come back through the same gateway's execution reports; cancels go the same way (the Requoter's cancel/replace). qip-edge-node's pass.rs tests run orders, cancels and fills with no mesh, Fabric or mirror constructed at all, and mesh.rs shows the cell keeps running with the centre unreachable. The Fabric itself does not exist yet (ADR 0100 has only just decided its first build), so 'no Fabric broker in between' holds vacuously. In the deployed loop, however, serve() (backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/main.rs:776-935) runs the journal flush to the configured store (cell.flush at :852) and the blocking mesh exchange with the centre (:869) synchronously on the same thread immediately before each run_pass (:888): a failure of either is logged and the pass still runs, but a slow sink or centre delays the pass by up to its I/O timeout. | PARTIAL | The requirement's own chaos check is not demonstrated: no test makes the journal sink and the regional/central services unreachable and then shows, in the same run, that orders and cancels still send and fills still book, and no test shows the journal catching up when the sink returns (mirror.rs never fails the store; cell.rs's flush tests are happy-path). The two separate tests show order flow with nothing else present and cell survival with the centre dead, which is a weaker property. In addition the only venue is the in-process simulator, so the 'order gateway' leg of the edge is a function call, and the deployed serve loop serialises a blocking flush and a blocking centre exchange ahead of every pass -- not 'in between' the order and the venue, but a synchronous dependency on the loop that drives the order path, which the requirement's rationale warns against and no test bounds. |  | P0 | cargo test -p qip-edge-node --test pass -- a_marketable_order_fills_on_the_pass_it_is_sent_once_the_venue_has_a_touch_to_take; cargo test -p qip-edge-node --test mesh -- a_tick_against_an_unreachable_centre_reports_it_and_leaves_the_cell_running | E04 |

Cell fills arriving over the mesh are booked instead to qip_capital::ledger::UserLedger per-strategy cash (book_settlement -> book_fill -> journal_to, platform.rs:5574,5653,5704) and to the risk aggregates (charge_cell_fills, platform.rs:8076-8094), never to TrackedCapital. A third copy, the desk's BookView { portfolio: Portfolio::new(..., initial_equity, now) } (platform.rs:4252-4259), is built once inside Arc<Desk>; only world and market are re-pointed at an Upstream (platform.rs:4241-4275), so the book slot has no writer, yet every agent holding Capability::ReadPortfolio reads positions and equity from it (qip-investment-agents construction.rs:109-120 turnover, 343-346 held count; review.rs:113-117 'the book already holds'). | TICK-001 | Raw market events never enter the cognitive context window | nothing — there is no 'cognitive layer' / context-window concept anywhere in the Rust workspace to trace inputs into. qip-reasoning-engine (the closest analogue, the REASON stage) reads no raw MarketMessage/SensedRecord/Topic::MarketTick* type (confirmed: rg for those symbols in crates/services/qip-reasoning-engine/src/*.rs outside tests returns nothing), so the prohibition holds today only vacuously, by absence of the thing it would forbid. | MISSING | There is no cognitive-layer context builder to write an architecture test against, and no test traces its inputs; the requirement's positive half (TICK-028, the closed representation-kind enum) is also missing, so the boundary is not yet a structural guarantee, only an accident of nothing having been built on that seam. | TICK-028 | P1 | An architecture test over the (not-yet-existing) cognitive-layer context builder's inputs, per the requirement's own check. | E09 |

The nearest kernel machinery — central::belief, central::causal, central::episodic (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/{belief,causal,episodic}.rs) — each derive one independent 'shipping-payload slot' for the centre-to-cell mesh (belief priors, a causal digest, an episodic digest), not a joined, time-aligned record carrying both world-side and market-side fields as TICK-002 defines them. | MISSING | No FusedRecord/fusion-layer type exists that carries both the world-side field list (events, entities, causal hypotheses, propagation paths) and the market-side field list (microstructure regime, liquidity, flow, lead/lag, execution feasibility) aligned to one as-of instant; the three central:: producers are single-purpose digests for the cross-cell mesh, not a fusion contract. | TICK-016, TICK-018 | P1 | The requirement's own property test over generated world and market streams; no analogue exists today. | E09 |
| TICK-003 | Event, receive and normalized time are never collapsed | Two parallel schemas disagree. qip_contracts::MarketMessage (backend/crates/libs/qip-contracts/src/message.rs:163-176) keeps venue_time and capture_time as distinct fields plus Origin{venue, sequence, partition} (venue.rs:141-150) — compliant in shape, but this type is reached only from the undeployed qip-edge-node and from tests (see TICK-014/015 rows). The type that actually reaches every deployed composition root — qip_market::quote::{Tick, Quote} (backend/crates/libs/qip-market/src/quote.rs:223-235) — carries exactly one timestamp field, `at`. Platform::observe, the SENSE-stage absorption function reached from every app (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs:8612), then writes that single timestamp into both the valid-time and known-time slots of the feature store: `FeatureValue::new(trade.price.to_f64(), trade.at, trade.at)` (platform.rs:8674-8684, and identically for Tick at :8686-8694) — collapsing event-time and receive-time into one value at exactly the seam this requirement protects. Two further seams confirm the collapse is structural rather than one call site: the connector runtime's MarketEventEnvelope does keep event_time, ingest_time and knowable_at apart (connector/envelope.rs:86-98, tested by connector_runtime.rs:759), but ConnectorFeed::poll strips the envelope to the bare SensedRecord (connector_feed.rs:477) before Platform::observe sees it; and the only decoder any composition root registers, qip-edge-node's DepthDecoder, stamps venue_time and capture_time with the same captured_at (qip-edge-node/src/feed.rs:414-426). | INCORRECT | The production-reached market-tick path has no receive time distinct from venue time, no normalized-time field, and no clock-uncertainty field; it treats a venue-stamped price as known the instant it happened, which this requirement names as exactly the corruption to prevent. |  | P0 | The requirement's property test over skewed venue/receive clocks, run against Platform::observe and qip_market::quote::{Tick,Quote} specifically, not against the unreached qip_contracts::MarketMessage. | E06 |

The only entitlement-adjacent concept in the tree, qip_financial::quality::LicensingClass, is stamped on captured SensedRecords at ingestion (e.g. backend/crates/services/qip-market-ingestion/src/service.rs:456) but is never propagated into a trained artifact's manifest. | MISSING | No mechanism records, on a trained artifact's manifest, which licensed data trained it or where it may run/be used, and nothing refuses to seal a manifest whose entitlement list is empty. | TICK-032 | P0 | The requirement's own integration test: a training run over two differently-entitled partitions produces a manifest listing both, and an empty-entitlement manifest is refused at seal time. | E08 |

| WORLD-001 | Disagreement between world models is recorded, not collapsed | nothing implements world-model-level disagreement recording. | REASON-001 | Symbolic conclusions never violate a declared invariant | nothing. No type anywhere in the workspace names a declared, versioned invariant set that symbolic conclusions are checked against. qip_reasoning_engine::redteam::RedTeam (backend/crates/services/qip-reasoning-engine/src/redteam.rs) performs a twelve-challenge adversarial review, but its Challenge/Severity model is heuristic evidence-quality critique (correlation-vs-causation, single-origin support, priced-in checks), not evaluation against a declared, versioned invariant list, and its rejection message names a challenge, never an invariant. | MISSING | No declared/versioned invariant registry exists anywhere in the fabric, and no reasoning path checks a conclusion against one or refuses naming the invariant broken. The red team's challenge list is the nearest structure and is not that: challenges are heuristics about evidence quality, not invariants the conclusion must preserve. |  | P0 | No test exists. Would need a fixture invariant registry, a checker run over every conclusion path (REASON, DECIDE), and a property test removing one invariant to prove the check can fire, per the requirement's own verification method. | E09 |
| REASON-002 | Consequential conclusions carry a machine-readable derivation | No unified 'derivation artifact' type (no SymbolicDerivation or equivalent exists anywhere). The four required parts exist scattered, unevenly, and only in qip_reasoning_engine's Bayesian pipeline: qip_reasoning_engine::hypothesis::Hypothesis carries an EvidenceSet (evidence set, part 2) and effective_confidence() (uncertainty, part 4); qip_reasoning_engine::redteam::ReviewOutcome carries a verdict and rationale naming which challenges stood (a loose analogue of 'assumptions found violated', part 3); qip_reasoning_engine::hypothesis::CausalChain narrates a mechanism chain (a loose analogue of a proof trace, part 1) but is prose (Hypothesis::narrate), not a machine-checkable rule/constraint/graph-path trace. No single type packages all four, and no promotion gate, risk check or capital decision reads such a combined artifact from the event log. | PARTIAL | No serde-serialisable type unifies proof trace, evidence set, violated assumptions and uncertainty into one artifact; the proof-trace half specifically (rules/constraints/graph paths applied, machine-checkable) does not exist anywhere. What exists is prose narration plus separately-typed evidence and confidence, not the artifact the requirement names. | REASON-001 | P0 | No test exists that replays a recorded reasoning run and asserts every consequential conclusion carries a 4-part derivation. The nearest test, backend/crates/services/qip-reasoning-engine/tests/reasoning.rs::confidence_is_computed_from_evidence_not_asserted (line 464), proves only the uncertainty part. | E09 |

| REASON-025 | Compiled reflex predicates are bounded | qip-strategy's compiler is exactly the 'refuse what cannot be bounded' compiler this row describes, for compiled strategies. It performs four checks. Declared inputs: every feature a strategy names must be declared in the FeatureCatalogue, or it is refused. Stated worst case: CompiledStrategy::cost() is the worst-case reachable node count, and above CompilerLimits::max_nodes (512 by default) the strategy is refused rather than trimmed; nesting beyond max_depth is refused too. No recursion: ir::Expr is a finite tree with no loop or call node, and Program::from_nodes refuses a node that reads itself or points forward. Runtime re-check: StrategyRuntime enforces a budget that does not grow with the program it is given, and Cell::deploy refuses a strategy whose cost exceeds the cell's strategy_budget. Evaluation cost does not depend on the market, and the acceptance performance suite measures it over firing and quiet vectors. What is missing: fabric-compiled predicates as the source; a per-artefact measurement over adversarial inputs asserted against that artefact's own declared bound; and a recursive predicate refused at compilation. Here recursion is unrepresentable in the IR rather than refused, and only the program-level check refuses a self-reading node. The assessor's rg included 'worst_case' over backend/crates/edge and reported no matches. It matches qip-strategy/tests/strategy.rs:255. | PARTIAL | The bound is proven for compiled strategies, not for fabric-compiled predicates. No test measures each artefact over adversarial inputs against its own declared bound (the performance test times one fixture against a wall-clock budget). Needed: a test that constructs a peer/cross-region channel alongside the downward path and re-asserts VerifiedPolicy/VerifiedHalt still refuse an unsigned or foreign-cell payload with that channel active. | E13 |

## RES

| Requirement | Blueprint target | Current implementation | Status | Gap | Dependency | Priority | Verification | Work item |

| RES-001 | A Fabric outage never stalls a live local decision | qip_edge::cell::Cell::on_bytes/Cell::work touch memory and arithmetic only (lib.rs module doc), and qip_edge::mesh::CellUplink pushes over qip_transport with retry/circuit-breaker/dead-letter. But the only composition root that runs a pass does not keep the decision off that path: qip-edge-node's serve loop runs cell.flush (journal shipping, main.rs:852), then the mesh exchange with the central plane (link.exchange_with_installers, main.rs:869: the uplink publish plus the capital and policy downlink polls, each over qip_transport with a 2 s connect / 15 s read timeout and a five-attempt backoff ladder that sleeps with ThreadSleeper), and only then run_pass (main.rs:888), one after another on one thread. A slow or black-holed centre link, or a stalled journal mirror, therefore delays the next decision until the timeouts, the retry ladder (about six seconds per message, by breaker.rs's own account) and the breakers let go. main.rs:863 calls this arrangement 'a compromise, not a design'. | INCORRECT | The integrated form is the synchronous dependency the requirement forbids. The reflex pass is sequenced behind network I/O to the Fabric's present analog (the centre mesh) and behind journal shipping, on the same thread, so an outage delays decisions rather than leaving them untouched. Closing it means taking the mesh exchange and the flush off the pass thread in qip-edge-node, or giving them a deadline the pass never waits on, and then proving it with a latency measurement. Separately, no native Event & Control Fabric exists (the blueprint's Tokio/QUIC/Raft design is ADR 0099 C2, refused). No chaos test kills every broker or forces a partition-leader failover and measures the tick-to-decision latency distribution against a no-fault band. |  | P0 | No test measures pass latency under an outage. backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/tests/mesh.rs::a_delta_for_a_peer_that_is_not_listening_is_dead_lettered_rather_than_blocking_forever and backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/tests/mesh.rs::a_tick_against_an_unreachable_centre_reports_it_and_leaves_the_cell_running both use a refused connection, which fails in milliseconds, and neither times the next pass. A black-holed peer (connect timeout) and a stalled read are not exercised. | E04 |
| RES-002 | A Reflex Mesh outage never stops durable journaling or control distribution | qip_edge::journal (FileMirror, hash-chained, Cell::flush) is code-independent of qip_edge::mesh (CellUplink/PolicyDownlink/CapitalDownlink) -- no shared failure path between the two, so a mesh push failure cannot stop a local journal write, and PolicyDownlink::poll (control distribution, downward) does not depend on CellUplink (state, upward) succeeding. | PARTIAL | The blueprint's peer 'Reflex Mesh' (cell-to-cell multi-leg coordination) does not exist as a layer distinct from the centre uplink/downlink modelled here -- qip_edge::mesh is the cell-to-centre channel, not a peer mesh (master Phase 4). No test partitions 'every Mesh link' of a cell and asserts every record it journals still reaches a Fabric mirror with contiguous offsets while a ControlPackAnnouncement is still received, as the verification method requires. In this tree, control distribution (PolicyDownlink, CapitalDownlink) and the state uplink both run over the one centre link, to the same peer. So losing that link does stop control distribution: there is no second path for control to arrive by. The journal is not affected, because qip-edge-node flushes before the exchange (main.rs:852) and logs a failed flush rather than raising it. |  | P1 | No test demonstrates the property. The cited tests/cell.rs::the_journal_chain_catches_an_edited_decision and ::mirror_batches_chain_onto_each_other_across_flushes prove the journal chain's integrity, not that journaling or control continues while a mesh link is partitioned. No test flushes the journal with a dead peer. | E11 |

Third, no single chaos run chains TTL, freshness and risk policy together. |  | P0 | backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/tests/cell.rs::an_expired_envelope_stops_the_cell_rather_than_letting_it_continue; tests/region_table.rs::a_partitioned_cell_keeps_spending_within_its_last_share_until_its_envelopes_expire; tests/telemetry.rs::a_policy_going_stale_narrows_the_cell_to_the_floor_and_the_gauges_move_with_it | E04 |

The nearest real mechanism is the cell's cached capital envelope. A cell's fills reach the centre's books only through its reports (CentralPlane::ingest -> settle/record_realised, plane.rs:2079). When the centre is unreachable, the cell keeps acting only within the signed VerifiedEnvelope it already holds, because the centre renews envelopes over the capital downlink and cannot while it is unreachable. Once that envelope expires, every new money-risking intent is refused under 'envelope_expiry' (cell.rs:3490-3500). The envelope's TTL is therefore the only bound on how long a cell acts unaccounted, and it is a fixed time, not a lag measurement. | PARTIAL | No ledger-commit-health signal exists.
